imp.smart1: • If the file has a Preamp: exactly that value is used, no double subtraction!

cf.title: Crossfeed Simulator (Bauer bs2b / Meier)
cf.desc: Removes the unnatural “inside the head” stereo isolation of headphones. It models the acoustic shadowing and delay of the head (ITD/ILD), so the music is heard in front of you, like from a real pair of studio monitors, rather than inside your ears.

lim.title: Limiter & True Peak Protection
lim.ovsTitle: Oversampling can be set in the Oversampling selector
lim.desc: Prevents boosts in the EQ or room correction from driving the DAC's analog reconstruction filter into digital clipping. The primary protection against clipping is a correct preamp (matched to the full EQ curve); the limiter is a safety net (it switches on automatically when a profile with a negative preamp is loaded) and is not a hearing protection device.
mono.title: Mono & subsonic cut
mono.desc: Subsonic cut: removes content below the selected frequency with a 24 dB/octave high-pass filter (rumble and speaker protection). Mono: blends the stereo bass below the cutoff frequency (default 100 Hz) into a common (summed) bass; the center channel does not change.
agc.title: Autogain
agc.desc: Automatic level matching: it steers the short-term (3 s) loudness to the target level, by at most the chosen amount. The change is slow (about 1 dB/s), so it does not pump.
agc.targetHint: Short-term loudness target (EBU R128, LUFS). Quiet material is raised towards it, loud material is lowered, within the limit below.
agc.maxGainHint: The largest gain increase and cut (dB). Silence (below -70 LUFS) does not change the gain.
bass.desc: For smaller speakers and bass-light headphones: rather than simply raising the level (which would cause cone distortion and rattling), it generates harmonics that the brain decodes as the presence of the low fundamental.

mt.desc: Automatic, restrained sound enhancer: it analyses the recording being played and only corrects what is missing or disturbing (boxy low-mids, dull highs, out-of-phase bass, narrow mix). It does not make things louder and does not compress: the output loudness matches the input.

ctl.magicAmountHint: 0 % = untouched signal; up to 100 % corrections stay within hard limits (see the Details). Above 100 %: “Bold” range with a stronger effect, audible on good recordings too.
ctl.monoAmountHint: Phase shift: below the cutoff the side bass is phase-rotated (at 100 % and a 100 Hz cutoff, about 90° at 50 Hz). The mono sum (center channel) does not change.
ctl.monoFreqHint: Bass up to this frequency is blended to mono (24 dB/octave Linkwitz–Riley filter). 80–120 Hz is typical; higher values also narrow the stereo image of instruments. There is no lower limit: the lowest band is handled by the subsonic cut.

mo.title: Multiple outputs
mo.zonesHint: Independent zones: each output plays with its own complete DSP chain (e.g. headphones with an AutoEq profile, speakers with room correction). Use the “Editing output” selector above to choose which output you adjust: every module, profile and import applies to that output.
mo.xoverHint: Active crossover: after the shared chain (output 1 settings) the signal is split into frequency bands (Linkwitz–Riley), and each output gets one band (e.g. subwoofer and satellites).
mo.mainDevice: the device chosen in the Output menu
mo.editingNote: You are editing output {n}: every module, profile and import applies to this output.
mo.note: Multiple outputs start switched off (the sound does not change); the settings and the outputs' profiles are kept. If you unplug a sound card, its output goes silent and does not play anywhere else.
os.title: Channels and dither
os.desc: If you don't sit in the middle between the speakers, delaying and lowering the nearer speaker puts the stereo image back in the centre. 1 ms of delay ≈ 34.3 cm of distance.
os.ditherDesc: The DSP chain calculates with far higher precision than the sound card accepts. Dither makes sure this precision carries over to the 16- or 24-bit output: quiet details, reverb tails and fade-outs stay clean and natural. It is standard practice in studio mastering and in serious audiophile players. It only runs when the chain changes the signal; an untouched signal stays bit-perfect.
os.modeOff: Off: no dither; the system rounds to the sound card's bit depth.
os.modeTpdf: TPDF: the most widely used, neutral kind, even across the whole audio band.
os.modeShaped: Noise-shaped: moves the remaining noise up to the highest frequencies, where hearing is least sensitive; at 16 bits this gives the cleanest sound.
os.modeTip: Which one? For a 24-bit sound card TPDF is perfect. At 16 bits (older USB DACs, 16-bit S/PDIF) noise-shaped is the better choice.
ctl.osBitsHint: What the sound card actually receives. If unsure, leave it at 24 bit.
ao.title: Sound output (advanced)
ao.keepAwakeHint: It doesn't sleep during silence: no pops, and the start of tracks isn't cut off.
ao.bitperfect: Bit-perfect: the DSP doesn't change the signal
ao.awake: The sound card is kept awake
ao.preloadHint: No disk or network reads during playback (e.g. a sleeping external drive, NAS).
ao.exclusiveHint: The player uses the sound card on its own: the Windows mixer and Equalizer APO are bypassed, the file plays at its own sample rate, and the DSP chain runs inside the program. Other programs can't play on this device meanwhile. Switching during playback briefly interrupts the sound.
ao.exclusiveAlsaHint: The player uses the DAC on its own: PipeWire releases it, the file plays at its own sample rate without conversion, the DSP chain runs inside the program and the volume is digital. Other programs can't play on this device meanwhile. Takes effect from the next track.
ao.exclusiveHogHint: The player uses the DAC on its own: the macOS audio system yields it, the file plays at its own sample rate without conversion, the DSP chain runs inside the program and the volume is digital. Other programs can't play on this device meanwhile. Takes effect from the next track.
ao.exclVolHint: Digital: the slider controls the level at the end of the program, the DAC's volume stays unchanged. Bit-perfect at 100%, not below. Hardware: the slider sets the DAC's own volume, which is bit-perfect, but it only works if the driver applies it in exclusive mode; if not, the slider has no effect. Takes effect from the next track.

loudness.desc: Equal-loudness contour correction (ISO 226 / Fletcher–Munson): compensates for the human ear's reduced sensitivity to low and high frequencies at lower volumes.
stereo.desc: Stereo imaging and spatial processing: stereo base, phase rotation, channel modes (Mid/Side), balance, and soft-clipping (Calf Stereo Tools).
ctl.loudVolumeHint: Listening volume: attenuates the overall signal by this amount while reducing bass and treble less according to equal-loudness curves, preserving full sound at lower volumes.
ctl.loudHclipHint: Hard clipping protection to prevent digital overshoot from dynamic boost within the specified decibel range.
ctl.stStereoBaseHint: Stereo image width: 0 is unchanged stereo, negative values narrow towards mono, positive values widen the stereo stage.
ctl.stSoftclipHint: Softclip: smoothly rounds off peaks (arctangent curve) so overdrive causes less harsh distortion. Level adjusts the saturation strength.

way.help: Per-way EQ runs after the shared EQ and affects only this speaker (for example, taming a subwoofer room resonance). Up to 10 bands are allowed, with boost capped at +6 dB to protect the driver.

ups.title: Upsampling (built-in player)
ups.presetReferenceHint: 99.7% bandwidth, 32-bit precision, linear phase. The most accurate, but needs the most computation.
ups.errStopbandRange: Stopband start must be between 100% and 150%.
ups.stopbandWarn: Above 100%, the filter closes above the Nyquist frequency, allowing slight aliasing in exchange for a gentler roll-off.
ups.errOrder: Bandwidth must be lower than the stopband start.
ups.statusWarnResample: Warning: the system resamples back to {actual} – enable exclusive mode or 'Follow source' sample rate
ups.statusUnsupported: No conversion: DAC does not support the target rate ({src})
ups.helpText: Upsampling raises the built-in player's PCM audio to a higher sample rate before playback. Phase controls pre- and post-ringing (0 = minimum phase, 25 = intermediate, 50 = linear), bandwidth sets the passband end, stopband start controls filter steepness (above 100% mild aliasing is permitted), and headroom adds margin for inter-sample peaks. Filter length and internal quality are derived automatically. Audible benefit depends on the DAC and is debated, so it is off by default. Engine: libsoxr, LGPL-2.1+.
la.title: High processor load
la.whyCpu: The audio engine has been using {cpu}% of the machine's capacity for a while.
la.whyXrun: Audio dropouts (underruns) occurred: {n} in the last 10 seconds.
la.step.two_threads: Suggestion: compute upsampling on two threads (the sound stays bit-identical).
la.step.precision24: Suggestion: lower the filter precision to 24 bit (less load; no practical difference on most DACs).
la.step.lower_target: Suggestion: use a lower target sample rate.
la.step.none: No further automatic step; close other programs or turn upsampling off.
la.doneText: A setting was changed; you can undo it if you don't like it.
la.setting: Tell me when processor load is high
la.settingHint: If the audio engine keeps the machine busy for long, or audio drops out, it offers a lighter setting. It never changes anything by itself.
hires.dspOff: At {rate} the DSP chain (EQ, filters) has no effect: the signal passes through unchanged, bit-perfect. The DSP works up to 384 kHz.
ups.threadsHint: With two threads the left and right channels are computed on separate cores. The result is bit-identical to single-thread; there is no audible difference. Only the load is shared, and high target rates come out more easily.
ups.coreHint: Pins the decoder thread to one processor core. It does not change the sound quality, at most it makes scheduling more predictable; most machines do not need it, so it is off by default.
ao.asio: ASIO output (through the DAC maker's driver)
ao.asioHint: The player plays through the DAC maker's ASIO driver: the Windows audio system and Equalizer APO are bypassed, the DSP chain runs inside the program, the volume is digital. Native DSD is used when the driver supports it. If ASIO does not start, the player falls back to WASAPI and the signal path shows why.
ao.asioNone: No ASIO driver is installed on this computer. If your DAC has one, install it from the maker's website, then reopen this menu.
ao.asioCredit: ASIO output (Windows): Steinberg ASIO SDK 2.3.4, GPLv3. ASIO is a trademark and software of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH.
ao.asioFallback: ASIO did not start ({reason}); the player uses WASAPI.
ao.asioErr_driver_not_found: the selected driver is not installed
ao.asioErr_invalid_clsid: invalid driver entry in the system
ao.asioErr_init_failed: the driver did not start (is the DAC off, or used by another program?)
ao.asioErr_channels: the driver has no two output channels
ao.asioErr_rate: the DAC does not support this sample rate
ao.asioErr_format: the driver's sample format is not supported
ao.asioErr_buffer: cannot start with the driver's buffer size
ao.asioErr_busy: this program already uses the ASIO driver
ao.asioErr_start_failed: the driver did not start playback
ao.asioErr_reset: the driver requested a restart; the player reopened it
ao.asioErr_device_lost: the DAC disappeared (unplugged or switched off)
ao.dsdNativeOn: Native DSD: {dsd}, {format} – the DAC receives the file's DSD stream bit-for-bit unchanged
ao.adminRequired: Changing these settings requires administrator permission. Grant it on the computer, in the Remote menu.
ao.exclRate: the DAC accepts this DSD rate neither natively nor over DoP (DSD1024 does not fit into DoP on any DAC); playing converted to PCM
er.privacyShort: When enabled, only sends the app version, system info, playback path, sound card model names, and recent engine log lines to the project server (stored for 90 days). Never sends your name, hostname, file paths, IP, MAC, or email address. You can turn it off anytime.
er.noteLabel: What were you doing right before? (optional, max 400 chars)
er.notePh: E.g. switched to a DSD track or turned on exclusive mode…
er.notConfigured: This build cannot send reports yet (reporting endpoint is not configured). Use “Save to file” instead.
er.sentOk: Error report sent, thank you. Reference ID: AQ-{id}
er.sendFailed: Could not send report ({reason}). You can use “Save to file” instead.
er.firstRunText: May Aqulify send anonymous error reports if something goes wrong? No personal data is sent.
er.prevBannerText: Last time Aqulify did not exit cleanly. Would you like to send what happened?
er.prevIntro: Summary of the previous abnormal run. Clicking “Send” gives one-time consent.
er.oneTimeHint: Clicking “Send” gives one-time consent for this report, even if automatic reporting is turned off.
